name: Rocco Forte Masseria Torre Maizza
insider_take: This 16th-century fortified farmhouse sits majestically on Puglia's Adriatic coast, where ancient olive groves meet crystalline waters and authentic Italian charm reigns supreme.
whats_special: The property features centuries-old olive trees that still produce the hotel's own extra virgin olive oil, while the original stone walls and watchtower tell stories of when it protected against Ottoman raids. The private beach club overlooks the same waters where ancient Greek sailors once navigated to establish nearby colonies.
pro_tip: Book the Trullo suites for an authentic Puglian experience - these traditional cone-roofed structures are UNESCO-recognized and offer the most romantic sunset views from your private terrace.
dont_miss: The hotel's cooking school in the ancient cistern, where you'll learn to make orecchiette pasta and burrata cheese using recipes passed down through generations of local families. The nearby town of Alberobello, just 20 minutes away, contains over 1,000 trulli houses - the largest concentration in the world.
pros: Historic 16th-century masseria with authentic Apulian architecture
Exclusive private beach club with direct Mediterranean access
World-class spa featuring traditional treatments and olive oil therapies
Exceptional Italian cuisine using local Pugliese ingredients
cons: Remote countryside location requires transportation to nearby attractions
